sentences.text:
This appeal arises out of the order dated 13.04.2018 in O.C. No. 853/2017 passed by the adjudicating authority under the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, as affirmed by the Appellate Tribunal under SAFEMA at New Delhi in appeal No.FPA-PMLA- 2368/CHN/2018 vide order dated 27.06.2024.
2.

The brief facts necessary for the disposal of the appeal are as follows:
By letter dated 26.03.2015 written by the UCO Bank Limited, a criminal complaint with the Central Bureau of Investigation, Anti- Corruption Branch, Chennai was registered as FIR RC MA-1/2015- A0012 dated 30.03.2015.

In the complaint, it is alleged that certain officials of the UCO Bank Limited had conspired with one Sri.L.Srinivasan (proprietor of VLS Mining) and Sri.K.Saravanan (partner in VLS Exports) to fraudulently provide an overdraft facility to VLS Mining against insufficient security, which resulted in an unpaid overdraft of Rs.5.09 crores.
The complaint also alleged that such officials had improperly sanctioned a loan of Rs.6.50 crores to VLS Exports without obtaining proper security.

The above allegations indicated the commission of offences under Section 120B read with 2025:KER:75189 MSA NO. 43 OF 2024 Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and also under Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Accordingly, a charge sheet was filed indicating commission of the aforesaid offences.

Finding that certain offences therein charged against the accused were identified as offences of money laundering as specified under Section 3 of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, the Enforcement Directorate registered a case as ECIR No.CEZO/02/2016 on 12.02.2016 to pursue a detailed investigation.
Pertinently, the appellant is an accused in neither of the above cases.

As a part of the investigation,
the appellant was summoned under sub- Sections (2) and (3) of Section 50 of the Prevention of Money- Laundering Act, 2002.
On 14.06.2017, the appellant appeared and gave evidence.
Thereafter, the respondent provisionally attached the funds along with certain other movables and immovable properties under P.A.O. No.20/2017 dated 25.10.2017.
Thereafter, the said order was confirmed.

sentences.text: the provisional order of attachment was objected to by the appellant, contending that the amounts sought to be attached are not proceeds of the crime and since he is not an accused in any of the complaints filed under the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, the proposal will not sustain.
The objections raised by the appellant were overruled, and order dated 13.04.2018 was passed by the adjudicating authority confirming the provisional order of attachment.
Aggrieved, an appeal 2025:KER:75189 MSA NO. 43 OF 2024 was preferred under Section 26 of the Prevention of Money- Laundering Act, 2002 against the order dated 13.4.2018.

The appeal was dismissed by order dated 27.6.2024, and hence, the present second appeal.
3. Heard Smt.Krishnapriya Sreekumar, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri.Jaishankar V. Nair, the learned Standing Counsel for the Enforcement Directorate.
4.
On 24.9.2025, this Court admitted the appeal and framed the following substantial questions of law for consideration:
"I. Whether the amount attached will come under the definition of "proceeds of crime" defined under Section 2(u) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002?

II. Whether the property attached will fall under the category "Attachment of property involved in money- laundering" under Section 5 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
 III.

The attached property is a credit balance of  Rs.5.73 lakhs (approx.) held in Account No.12790100076365 held by the Appellant with Federal Bank, Irinjalakuda, Kerala.
The attached property is the payout received by the Appellant from Sree Gokulam Chit and Finance Co.Pvt.Ltd. upon the maturing of an 2025:KER:75189 MSA NO. 43 OF 2024 investment made by the Appellant.

entities.text: Sree Gokulam Chit and Finance Co.Pvt.Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The attached property is wholly unconnected to the PMLA offence and has been attached solely as the equivalent value of alleged proceeds of crime received by the Appellant.

IV. Whether the transferred amounts received by the appellant from the accused in the crime out of the credit facility availed from Canara Bank be attached in a proceeding against the said person under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002?"
5.
The learned counsel appearing for the appellant primarily contended that the amount attached cannot be considered as proceeds of crime.
The funds received from the accused were clearly exhausted by 20.09.2014.
The amounts transferred into the account of the appellant by the accused were obtained by operating an overdraft account with the Canara Bank.
The details of such account were clearly available before the adjudicating authority as well as before the Appellate Tribunal.

sentences.text: the intention of the respondent was to recover the proceeds of the crime which had come into the account of the accused, then necessary proceedings ought to have been taken against Canara Bank for reversing the various credit entries in the overdraft facility operated by the accused with them.

Since the Canara Bank was not arrayed as a respondent in the proceedings, the funds received out of the operation of the account of the accused in 2025:KER:75189 MSA NO. 43 OF 2024 the overdraft facility with Canara Bank cannot be termed as the proceeds of the crime.

6. Per contra, Sri.Jaishankar V. Nair, the learned Standing Counsel for the Enforcement Directorate,
supported the findings of the adjudicating authority as well as the Appellate Tribunal.

According to him, in the course of investigation, the Enforcement Directorate had discovered that one Sri.L.Srinivasan had received large inward remittances in the guise of export advances and had diverted those remittances for purposes other than export.

The investigation further revealed that the amounts received by Sri.Jibu Paul are certainly the proceeds of the crime and therefore, the further remittance by Sri.Jibu Paul into the account of the appellant can clearly be brought under the definition of the proceeds of the crime.

He further submitted that the appellant had admitted that he received two bank transfers on 17.06.2014 and 24.07.2014 in his NRO account and that the appellant failed to prove his contention that the said amounts received in his account were in fact for return of the loan amount and therefore, the amount represents the value of the proceeds of the crime and thus, the order of attachment for Rs.5,73,859/- was rightly confirmed by the adjudicating authority as well as by the Appellate Tribunal.

7. I have considered the rival submissions raised across the bar and given anxious consideration to the findings rendered by the 2025:KER:75189 MSA NO. 43 OF 2024 adjudicating authority as well as by the Appellate Tribunal.
8. At the outset, this Court takes note of the remiss that occurred at the hands of the adjudicating authority as well as of the Appellate Tribunal.

The evidence in the form of Bank statements, which indicated the transfer of the alleged proceeds of the crime into the account of Sri.Jibu Paul,
operating in the form of an Overdraft facility with Canara Bank, was clearly made available before the authorities.
In fact, the learned counsel for the appellant had produced the said statements before this Court also.
The learned counsel for the respondent does not dispute the veracity of the Bank statements.

A perusal of the Bank statements shows that Rs.1.2 Crores was received on 12.6.2014 and the Canara Bank utilised the said amount to make up the deficit in the account, which was lying at a negative balance of Rs.89,90,340/- and on receipt of this amount and after adjustment of the amounts, the balance in the account of Sri.Jibu Paul falls short of Rs.35,09,640/-.
After effecting a series of transactions, the account again went on a negative balance and it was thereafter the account was operated, and the amounts in question were sent to the appellant herein.

The relevant entries showing the transfer of Rs. 5 lakhs and Rs. 2 lakhs happened on 17.06.2014 and 24.07.2014, and by that time, the account was showing a negative balance of Rs.6,65,531/- and Rs.31,06,864/-, respectively.

Thus, it is explicitly clear that, what was transferred into the account of the 2025:KER:75189 MSA NO. 43 OF 2024 appellant is not the proceeds of the crime, but by operating the credit facility offered by Canara Bank to Sri.Jibu Paul.

4 9.

entities.text: Francis Chakkalamattom Peter vs Deputy Director on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There was no explanation offered by the Department either before the Appellate Tribunal or before this Court as to why proceedings were not taken against Canara Bank, and also against the persons to whom Sri.Jibu Paul made the transactions from the overdraft facility availed from Canara Bank.

If the intention of the Department was to secure back the proceeds of the crime, which was received by Sri.Jibu Paul, necessary steps ought to have been taken against Canara Bank, and directions ought to have been issued to them to reverse the entries made under the overdraft facility in order to retrieve the proceeds of Rs.1.2 Crores deposited into the account of Sri.Jibu Paul.
Having not taken these steps, this Court fails to comprehend as to how the adjudicating authority could attach the amount of Rs.5,73,859/-, considering the value of the proceeds of the crime.
Therefore, it is clear that the provisional attachment effected by the adjudicating authority and confirmed by the Appellate Tribunal is clearly without jurisdiction.

The Appellate Tribunal, which is constituted to review the action taken by the adjudicating authority under the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, has given a complete go by to the aforesaid transactions and the basic tenets governing the operation of an overdraft facility.
It is immaterial as to under which head the appellant received the amount of Rs.7 lakhs 2025:KER:75189 MSA NO. 43 OF 2024 from Sri.Jibu Paul.

So long as the appellant had produced the necessary documents to show that the amounts were transferred by Sri.Jibu Paul by operating the Overdraft facility available with Canara Bank, then, the entire edifice of the case set up by the adjudicating authority to proceed against the appellant collapses.

10. In view of the discussion above, this Court is inclined to answer the substantial questions of law as follows:
I. The amount attached will not come under the definition of proceeds of crime as defined under Section 2(u) of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002.

II. The property attached will not fall under the category of "attachment of property in money laundering" under Section 5 of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act,
2002.
III. The attached property will not come within the equivalent value of the alleged proceeds of the crime.

IV. The amount transferred and received by the appellant from the credit facility availed by the accused cannot be attached in proceedings under the provisions of the Prevention of Money- Laundering Act, 2002.

Resultantly, the second appeal is allowed by setting aside the order dated 13.04.2018 in O.C. No. 853/2017 passed by the adjudicating authority under the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, and as affirmed by the Appellate Tribunal under S A F E M A a t 2 0 2 5 : K E R : 7 5 1 8 9 M S A N O . 4 3 O F 2 0 2 4 N e w D e l h i i n FPA-PMLA-2368/CHN/2018 by final order dated 27.6.2024.
Consequently, the order of attachment dated 25.10.2017 and its affirmation by the adjudicating authority in OC No.853/2017 PMLA dated 13.04.2018 will stand set aside.
There will be a direction to the respondent to return the attached property to the appellant within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.
